title: Per-route alerting, exportable views, and debug CSV wireframe (WIP)
body:
Summary:

This is a working doc capturing UX notes and quick wireframe ideas for two related features we need to deliver together: 1) per-route/per-key alerting (threshold and anomaly detection) and 2) exportable debug datasets (CSV/NDJSON) for usage and rate-limit incidents. The aim is to make it straightforward for platform engineers and SREs to diagnose quota breaches and for product customers to set up sensible guards without drowning in noisy alerts.

Goals and success metrics:
- Allow customers to create targeted alerts for routes and API keys (by route-prefix, method, or tag) that map to quota/rate-limit policies.
- Provide a one-click export for the last N minutes/hours of traffic for a key+route with token-level metrics (tokens generated, latency p50/p95, model variant, cost estimate).
- Reduce support time for investigating rate-limit incidents by 50% (measured by internal ticket TTR).
- Reduce noisy alerts via easy-to-configure aggregation windows and anomaly sensitivity.

Personas:
- Platform Engineer (internal): Needs raw data to debug model fallbacks, routing, and capacity issues. Wants CSV/NDJSON with request_id, timestamp, route, key, token_counts, latency, model_version, region, and fallback_reason.
- Customer SRE/SE: Wants targeted alerts and a lightweight export to share with their team. Prefers pre-filtered downloads (by route and time) and clear attribution of cost.
- Product Manager / Billing Analyst: Needs per-route cost estimates in exports to reconcile spikes.

Primary flows (high level):
1) Create alert flow:
- Top-level: Alerts -> New alert -> Choose scope (Organization-wide / Key / Route / Key+Route).
- Scope selection UI: breadcrumb-style selector (Org > Project > Key > Route pattern).
- Condition: metric selector (requests/min, tokens/min, errors/min, 429-rate, cost/min) + aggregation window (1m/5m/1h) + comparator (+ absolute or percent baseline).
- Sensitivity: toggle between Static Threshold and Adaptive (baseline + sigma multiplier). Adaptive uses rolling 7-day baseline by default.
- Actions: webhook, email, pagerduty, console-notification, auto-throttle (experimental).
- Preview: show the last 24h chart for chosen metric and the proposed threshold marker.

Notes on UI behavior and tradeoffs for alerts:
- Progressive disclosure: hide advanced options (baseline window, smoothing, seasonality) under "Advanced" so quick users can set up simple alerts.
- Defaults: for new alerts on a route, default to a 5m aggregation window and static threshold at x2 of current 95th percentile to avoid immediate firing.
- Rate-limit auto-throttle: if enabled, the system reduces burst capacity for the offending key for a short cooldown. Must be opt-in and clearly labeled.
- Multi-route alerting: allow grouping by route-tag (customers may tag routes like /chat/* or /embeddings/*).

2) Inspect + export flow (one-click debug download):
- From any per-route/per-key dashboard card, show an "Export debug data" button. Clicking opens a small modal with filters: time range (quick presets), max rows (10k default), include/omit payloads (sensitive), redaction level (none/PII-hash/remove).
- Export types: CSV (wide table), NDJSON (one event per line), or Parquet (for large datasets).
- Columns exported (minimum recommended): timestamp, request_id, project_id, api_key_id (hashed depending on tenant export), route, model_variant, prompt_token_count, completion_token_count, total_tokens, response_latency_ms, http_status, error_code, cost_estimate_usd, region, routing_decision, fallback_reason.
- Additional advanced column toggles: client_ip (redacted default), user_metadata (JSON blob, redacted by default), raw_prompt_snippet (first 512 chars with redaction option).

Wireframe sketch (text) for the export modal:
----------------------------------------------------------------
| Export debug data for: "/chat/v1/message" (api_key: ********)      |
| Time range: [Last 1h v] [custom start/end]                        |
| Max rows: [10000]  Export format: (o) CSV  ( ) NDJSON  ( ) Parquet   |
| Include: [x] cost_estimate [x] routing_decision [ ] raw_prompt     |
| Redaction: ( ) None  (x) Hash keys  ( ) Remove PII                 |
| [Preview 20 rows]  [Download now]  [Save preset]                   |
----------------------------------------------------------------

Data model & export semantics (important):
- api_key_id in CSV: hashed by default when exported by customers; internal exports include full id but require IAM permission.
- cost_estimate_usd: calculated using the model version and token unit price at the time of request (show rounding and method).
- routing_decision & fallback_reason: helpful for diagnosing throttles and regional fallbacks. Be explicit about enum values in export header.
- Time alignment: timestamps exported in UTC ISO8601. Include original epoch_ms for sorting.

Edge cases and privacy considerations:
- GDPR/Pii: default export settings must not include full client_ip or raw prompt content. Add an inline warning if raw_prompt_snippet is requested.
- Cross-tenant exports: disallow exports that include data from multiple tenants unless the user has owner-level permission.
- Large exports: if >100k rows, queue job and notify via webhook/email when ready. Provide sample S3/GS link expiry rules.

Alerting visualizations / per-route dashboard layout ideas:
- Top row: small KPI tiles (requests/min, tokens/min, error_rate, 429_rate, est_cost/hr) with color-coded health.
- Mid row: per-route time-series with stacked breakdown by api_key (top 5) and hover drill to open an inspect panel.
- Bottom row: recent incidents with a quick "attach debug export" CTA that builds a time-limited export pre-filtered to the incident window.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UI to create alerts scoped to route and/or key with static and adaptive modes.
- Export modal that allows filtering by time and choosing CSV/NDJSON, with default PII-safe settings.
- Export includes at least the required columns and produces a downloadable file (sync for small, async for big exports).
- RBAC: only users with export permission can include non-redacted identifiers.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Adaptive baseline algorithm: rolling mean + 3 sigma? Or use median absolute deviation for robustness? (ask Applied ML for guidance)
- Cost column granularity: do we include model pricing tags per-token in the export? (billing team input)
- Should exports allow anonymized grouping (e.g., aggregate by hashed_key) to enable sharing with third parties?
- Naming: "Export debug data" vs "Download incident dump" — which is clearer for customers?

Next steps / rough backlog (tickets to spin):
- UX: high-fidelity mockups and copy for export modal (owner: Maya) JIRA: CONSOLE-912
- Backend: export job API + signed URL staging (owner: Ethan) JIRA: INF-4873
- Alerts: wire up adaptive baseline algo and provide metrics preview API (owner: Priya) JIRA: CONSOLE-928
- Security review: export PII flows and RBAC matrix (owner: Security) JIRA: SECU-303

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: prioritize a clear export with PII-safe defaults and minimal friction for incident owners. Focus on avoiding immediate alert noise with sane defaults and preview.
- I want quick feedback on the export columns and the redaction defaults from Billing and Security.

Reference quick links:
- Existing per-key analytics card: /product/console/cards/per-key-usage (reference)
- Billing price list: /confluence/Billing/TokenPricing

-- Jordan
(early draft)
